name: Liver FNA cytology – proposed WHO liver scheme (in preparation; not a published WHO book)
edition: Consensus/proposed – no WHO liver cytopathology book published

items: Representative lesional cells; cell block for IHC.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic neuroendocrine tumour
diagnoses.final: Malignant (Liver FNA (proposed scheme)). Metastatic neuroendocrine tumour.
diagnoses.comment: Monotonous plasmacytoid cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin; synaptophysin/chromogranin, Ki-67 for grade; search for GEP primary.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Liver FNA (proposed scheme) – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Hepatoblastoma
diagnoses.comment: Paediatric; fetal/embryonal small hepatoid cells ± mesenchymal elements; glypican-3/β-catenin; serum AFP.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Liver FNA (proposed scheme) – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma
diagnoses.comment: Discohesive atypical lymphoid cells with lymphoglandular bodies; send for flow cytometry and cell block IHC.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: Liver FNA (proposed scheme) – Malignant

extra.title: Status
items: The literature refers to a 'proposed WHO Reporting System for Liver Cytopathology' with 5 categories (Insufficient/Inadequate/Non-diagnostic, Benign, Atypical, Suspicious, Malignant). No liver book appears in the WHO Classification of Tumours online cytopathology series (checked Oct 2026).
ROM is not established by WHO; figures are from individual studies applying the proposed categories.

references: Navigating the horizon: The World Health Organization reporting system for liver cytopathology (ScienceDirect, 2024; pii S2772736X24000094).
Risk of Malignancy and Overall Survival Across Diagnostic Categories of the New WHO Reporting System in Liver Cytopathology. Lab Invest. 2024 (abstract 345).
Classifying Liver Cytology Using the WHO Reporting System: Institutional Experience and Malignancy Risk Assessment. Diagn Cytopathol. 2025 (doi 10.1002/dc.70112).
WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Digestive System Tumours. 5th ed. IARC, 2019.
